trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Use this time to rest on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport at 13:00. Take the Aerobus (€5.90 one-way) or Metro L9 Sud (€5.15) to the city center. Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. Once settled, take a leisurely self-guided walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — spot Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside (free). Great introduction to Barcelona's Modernisme architecture without spending a euro.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Eixample neighborhood on foot. Head to Carrer del Consell de Cent or Carrer de Muntaner for a taste of local bar culture. Enjoy your first 'vermut' (vermouth) at a neighborhood bar — a classic Barcelona tradition. Stroll around and get your bearings before an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick bocadillo (sandwich) at the airport for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh sandwich or slice of pizza near the hotel from a local bakery or supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl nearby) for €3–6.
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved local spot in Eixample with excellent tapas (patatas bravas, croquetas). Budget €12–16 per person. Arrive before 8pm to avoid long queues.

day_by_day.notes: August in Barcelona is hot (30°C+). Stay hydrated, carry a reusable water bottle (public fountains are drinkable), and wear sunscreen. The Metro is the most budget-friendly way to get around (T-Casual 10-trip card costs ~€11.35 and works on metro, bus, and tram).

day_by_day.morning: Start the day early (before the heat peaks) with a visit to the Sagrada Família. Book tickets online in advance to save time and potentially get a cheaper slot — basic entry is around €26, tower access extra. Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring Gaudí's extraordinary basilica, the ultimate symbol of Barcelona's architectural ambition. The morning light through the stained glass on the Nativity façade side is stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to Park Güell (Metro L3 to Vallcarca or Lesseps). The Monumental Zone requires a ticket (~€10, book online). Explore the famous mosaic terrace, dragon staircase, and hypostyle room. The surrounding free park area offers great views of the city — bring a picnic lunch to eat on the hillside. After Park Güell, head back to the hotel for a midday rest during the hottest hours (2–4pm).
day_by_day.evening: Head to El Born / Sant Pere neighborhood (Metro L4 Barceloneta or L1 Arc de Triomf). Wander the medieval streets and browse the architecture of the Santa Maria del Mar basilica (free entry or small donation). As night falls, explore the buzzing bar scene on Carrer del Parlament or Carrer del Rec. This area is a nightlife hotspot — bar-hop and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere until late.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at a local café near the hotel. Eixample has dozens of neighborhood cafés — look for a 'café amb llet' (café con leche) and a tostada for €2.50–4.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local market or supermarket — bread, cheese, jamón, fruit — and eat at Park Güell. Total cost: €5–8.
meals.dinner: Bar del Pla in El Born — excellent traditional Catalan tapas at honest prices. Try the foie gras with apple or the croquetas. Budget €13–18 per person with a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online at least a few days in advance — they sell out fast in August. Wear comfortable walking shoes; today involves a lot of uphill walking near Park Güell.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) — one of the best free experiences in Barcelona. Explore the labyrinthine medieval streets, the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30pm and after 5:30pm), the Pont del Bisbe bridge, Plaça Reial, and the Roman ruins visible through the streets. This is a walker's paradise and completely free. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down La Rambla toward the waterfront and visit the Boqueria Market (La Mercat de la Boqueria) — great for browsing and picking up affordable fresh fruit, nuts, and snacks (avoid the touristy prepared food stalls which are overpriced). Continue to Barceloneta Beach for a swim and relaxation — the beach is free and only 20 minutes on foot from the Gothic Quarter. Rent a sunbed if desired (~€6) or just use your towel on the sand.
day_by_day.evening: As the sun sets, walk up to the Barceloneta promenade. Enjoy the golden hour views. Then head to the Poble Sec neighborhood (Metro L2 Paral·lel) — home to the famous Carrer de Blai, Barcelona's 'pintxos street.' Sample pintxos (Basque-style tapas on bread) for €1–2 each at multiple bars. This is one of the best budget eating experiences in the city. Afterward, explore Poble Sec's growing nightlife scene — check out Sala Apolo or nearby bars for live music or DJ sets.

meals.breakfast: Granja Viader near the Gothic Quarter — a historic Barcelona café open since 1870. Try the 'suís' (hot chocolate with cream) and a pastry for €4–6.
meals.lunch: Fresh fruit and snacks from La Boqueria + a bocadillo from a side-street café near the waterfront. Budget €5–8.
meals.dinner: Carrer de Blai pintxos crawl in Poble Sec. Visit 3–4 bars and enjoy 5–8 pintxos with a beer or glass of wine. Budget €10–14 per person for a very satisfying meal.

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is extremely crowded in August — go before 11am if possible. Beware of pickpockets on La Rambla and at the beach; keep valuables secure. Barceloneta can get very busy — arrive before 1pm to claim a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Montjuïc (Metro L3 Paral·lel + Funicular, included in T-Casual card). Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (~€14 entry) or save money and explore the free outdoor areas and gardens of Montjuïc. Walk up to the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry, free on Sundays after 3pm) for panoramic views over the city, the port, and the sea. Spend 2 hours exploring the castle grounds and taking in the views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back down to the city via the cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc, ~€9 one-way) for a scenic ride — or take the free funicular back down. Visit the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe (Barcelona Pavilion) — a masterpiece of modernist architecture built for the 1929 World Exhibition, entry ~€7. This is a must-see for architecture lovers. Afterward, relax in the nearby Parc de Joan Miró (free) before heading back to the hotel for a siesta.
day_by_day.evening: Tonight, experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife. The city truly comes alive after midnight. Start with dinner in Eixample, then head to the Gràcia neighborhood (a 10-minute walk from Eixample) for pre-drinks at a local bar on Plaça del Sol or Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia — very popular with locals. Later, head to a club in the Eixample or Poble Sec area. Look for free entry before midnight or check for guest-list options online. Popular budget-friendly clubs include Sala Apolo and Nitsa Club.

meals.breakfast: Café and tostada con tomate (toast with tomato and olive oil — the quintessential Catalan breakfast) at a neighborhood bar near the hotel. €3–5.
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or grab a bocadillo to eat on Montjuïc. Alternatively, the Montjuïc area has a few café kiosks — budget €6–9.
meals.dinner: Federal Café or a local menú del día (set lunch/dinner menu) in Eixample. Many restaurants offer a 3-course menú del día for €10–14 including bread and a drink — outstanding value. Look for handwritten blackboard menus outside restaurants.

day_by_day.notes: The menú del día is one of the best budget hacks in Barcelona — look for it at lunch (1–3:30pm) and occasionally at dinner. Barcelona nightlife starts very late; clubs don't fill up until 1–2am. Pace yourself and consider a short nap in the afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most spectacular pieces of Modernisme architecture in the world, designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Guided tours cost around €22 or you can attend a morning concert for a similar price (check the schedule online — attending a performance is the most immersive way to experience the space). Alternatively, admire the exterior for free and snap photos of the extraordinary mosaic façade.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to any neighborhoods or sights you loved earlier in the trip, or explore the Gràcia district on foot — a charming, bohemian neighborhood with independent shops, colorful tiled squares (Plaça de la Virreina, Plaça del Diamant), and a very local feel. Visit the Casa Vicens (Gaudí's first major work, ~€16 entry) — far less crowded than Sagrada Família but equally fascinating for architecture lovers. Do some last-minute souvenir shopping at local shops rather than tourist traps — the Eixample and Gràcia areas have great independent stores.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final sunset walk along Passeig de Gràcia or head to the Bunkers del Carmel (free, 30-min walk or short taxi from Gràcia) — a hilltop Civil War anti-aircraft battery that offers the best 360° panoramic views of Barcelona, especially at sunset. A beloved local secret. End the trip with a farewell dinner in Eixample, savoring your last taste of Catalan cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a proper sit-down breakfast at a café in the Gothic Quarter or Eixample — try 'pa amb tomàquet' (bread with tomato) and fresh orange juice. €5–8.
meals.lunch: Menú del día at a local restaurant in Gràcia neighborhood. Budget €11–14 for a full 3-course meal with drink.
meals.dinner: La Pepita in Gràcia — a beloved local spot known for creative, affordable montaditos (small open sandwiches). Lively atmosphere, great for a festive final night. Budget €12–16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: If your departure flight is the next morning, pack your bags tonight and check transport options to the airport in advance. The Aerobus runs from Plaça de Catalunya and is the easiest option (€5.90). Keep your T-Casual card if you have trips remaining — it's valid for the metro to the airport on Line L9. Leave time to enjoy your last evening without rushing.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Barcelona Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample by taxi or Aerobus (~35–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll along Passeig de Gràcia, the grand boulevard right in Eixample, to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — three rival Modernista masterpieces (Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, Casa Lleó Morera) from the outside. Window-shop and soak in the architecture at a relaxed pace to beat jet lag.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the nearby Eixample Esquerra or Gràcia border for a casual first dinner. Explore the lively Carrer del Consell de Cent or Carrer de Muntaner bar scene for a pre-dinner vermouth (vermut) at a traditional bodega.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a coffee and croissant at the hotel or a nearby café upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick bocadillo or grab a menú del día (set lunch) at a local Eixample café near the hotel — budget €12–16 per person.
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — beloved local spot for tapas and montaditos. Mid-range, expect €25–35 per person with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — arrival fatigue is real in August heat. Stay hydrated. Pick up a T-Casual metro card (10 trips) at the airport or a metro station to save on transport costs throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour (pre-booked skip-the-line ticket essential — book in advance). Spend 2–2.5 hours exploring Gaudí's iconic basilica with a guide who will illuminate the symbolism of the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like interior columns, and the ongoing construction story. Arrive at opening time (~9:00) to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short metro ride to Park Güell and the Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration. Explore the mosaic terraces, the dragon staircase, and Hypostyle Room in the monumental zone (timed ticket required). Afterward, wander down into the charming Gràcia neighborhood — browse its village-like squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for a relaxed evening. Enjoy a sunset drink on a rooftop bar — try the rooftop at Hotel Pulitzer or the terrace at Casa Fuster for skyline views. Then head out for a proper sit-down dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Federal Café (Carrer del Parlament) or a local Eixample bakery — coffee, toast with tomato (pa amb tomàquet), and fresh orange juice. ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Grab a menú del día near Park Güell or in Gràcia — a 3-course lunch with wine for €13–18 per person at a neighborhood restaurant.
meals.dinner: Parking Pizza (Carrer de Londres, Eixample) — beloved upscale-casual spot with creative pizzas and natural wines. ~€25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: August is peak season — both Sagrada Família and Park Güell MUST be booked online weeks in advance. Wear comfortable shoes for lots of walking. Carry water; temperatures in Barcelona in August regularly exceed 30°C (86°F).

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour — join a guided walking tour through Barcelona's medieval heart. Discover Roman walls, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, the old Jewish quarter (El Call), and hidden courtyards. Most tours run 2–2.5 hours starting around 10:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Gothic Quarter tour, cross into the adjacent El Born neighborhood for the Tapas and Wine Tour. This guided tapas crawl takes you through El Born's best pintxos bars and wine stops, sampling patatas bravas, jamón, anchovies, and local Catalan wines. Tours typically run 13:00–16:00.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening freely in El Born and La Barceloneta. Walk down to the beach for a sunset stroll. Grab a drink at a beach bar (chiringuito) as the sun sets over the Mediterranean. This is a great night to turn in early or stay out late at your own pace.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Café de l'Acadèmia near the Gothic Quarter or at your hotel before heading out — coffee, croissant, and fresh juice. ~€8–10.
meals.lunch: Covered by the Tapas and Wine Tour (included in tour price, typically €65–85 per person). This replaces a standalone lunch.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet (Carrer de Montcada, El Born) — a legendary cava bar and tapas spot with house cava and anchovies. Very atmospheric. ~€20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter and El Born are walkable from each other — no transport needed between them. Beware of pickpockets in the Gothic Quarter tourist areas; keep bags in front. The tapas tour is a highlight — confirm booking in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Free morning for independent architecture exploration. Walk the Eixample grid and seek out lesser-known Modernista gems: Casa Vicens (Gaudí's first major work), Palau del Baró de Quadras, and the Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau (a stunning UNESCO-listed hospital complex by Domènech i Montaner — a must for architecture lovers). Allow 1.5–2 hours at Sant Pau.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Montjuïc hill for the afternoon. Take the cable car or bus up to explore the Fundació Joan Miró (world-class modern art in a beautiful rationalist building by Josep Lluís Sert) and the Jardins de Laribal. Enjoy sweeping views of the city and port from the castle or the Mirador del Migdia.
day_by_day.evening: Tonight is your Nightclub Experience on Passeig Marítim. Pre-game with dinner near Barceloneta, then head to the beachfront club strip. Visit iconic venues like Pacha, Opium, or Shôko. Clubs typically don't fill up until 01:00–02:00, so pace yourself. Dress code applies at most venues.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Alsur Café (Carrer de Londres) — avocado toast, eggs, smoothies. A popular Eixample brunch spot. ~€14–18.
meals.lunch: Menú del día near Sant Pau or Montjuïc — try a traditional Catalan restaurant in the Sarrià or Poble Sec neighborhood for €14–18.
meals.dinner: Barraca (Passeig Marítim de la Barceloneta) — seafood-forward restaurant right on the beachfront, perfect for pre-club dinner. Paella, grilled fish, and cocktails. ~€35–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: For the nightclub, buy tickets or get on the guest list online in advance to avoid long queues and cover charges. Clubs are open until 05:00–06:00. Take a taxi or Uber home — night buses exist but are slower. Budget €20–40 for club entry and €10–15 per cocktail inside.

day_by_day.morning: Slow recovery morning after the nightclub evening. Sleep in, then enjoy a leisurely late breakfast. Take a final walk along the Rambla de Catalunya (the more elegant, tree-lined version of La Rambla) and browse the Mercat de l'Eixample or pop into any last shops or galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palau de la Música Catalana (a UNESCO-listed Modernista concert hall by Domènech i Montaner) — book a guided tour or attend a rehearsal if available. The stained-glass skylight and ornate interior are breathtaking. Afterward, revisit El Born for any last souvenir shopping or café time.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in style — choose a restaurant that reflects the trip's highlights. Then take a last evening walk along the illuminated Passeig de Gràcia to say goodbye to the city's iconic architecture lit up at night.

meals.breakfast: Late brunch at Cosmo (Carrer d'Enric Granados) — a relaxed café on Barcelona's most beautiful pedestrian street. Eggs, pastries, coffee. ~€12–16.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Bar Calders (Carrer del Parlament, Sant Antoni) — a beloved neighborhood bar with excellent tapas and vermouth. ~€15–20.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda (Carrer de Sepúlveda, Eixample) — a cozy wine bar and restaurant with excellent Catalan cuisine and an impressive wine list. Perfect farewell dinner. ~€35–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: If departing the next morning, pack bags tonight and confirm transport to the airport. The Aerobus from Plaça de Catalunya takes ~35 minutes to the airport. Enjoy a final vermouth or nightcap on the hotel terrace or at a nearby bar — Barcelona's magic is best savored slowly.

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Barcelona Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private transfer arranged from El Prat Airport to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample via luxury chauffeur service. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your suite.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely stroll along Passeig de Gràcia directly from the hotel — admire the iconic 'Block of Discord' featuring Casa Batlló and Casa Amatller from the exterior. Stop for a private guided facade tour of Casa Batlló (premium access available without full interior queue). Browse the elegant boutiques and soak in the Eixample's grand Modernista streetscape.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Disfrutar (2 Michelin stars, just a short taxi from Eixample) — one of the world's top avant-garde restaurants offering a creative tasting menu rooted in Catalan tradition. Book the premium tasting menu with wine pairing. After dinner, unwind with cocktails at the rooftop bar of the Mandarin Oriental on Passeig de Gràcia — stunning city views to close your first night.

meals.lunch: Light welcome lunch at Parking Pizza or a charcuterie and cava spread arranged by the hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Disfrutar — avant-garde Catalan tasting menu with sommelier-selected wine pairing (reserve well in advance)

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Confirm Casa Batlló facade/exterior tour timing. Disfrutar reservations should be booked months ahead for this caliber of dining. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Skip-the-line Sagrada Família Guided Tour — book a premium private guided experience including tower access. Spend 2–3 hours marveling at Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece, exploring the Nativity and Passion facades, the luminous interior nave, and the museum crypt. A private guide will provide architectural and historical context unavailable on standard tours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell and Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — private car transfer to Park Güell for a guided tour of the mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and the panoramic city viewpoints. Afterward, descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood for a relaxed walk through its bohemian plazas, artisan shops, and café terraces. Visit Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Alkimia in Eixample — a celebrated Michelin-starred restaurant offering refined contemporary Catalan cuisine. Chef Jordi Vilà's seasonal tasting menu is a masterclass in local ingredients elevated to luxury. Post-dinner, enjoy a nightcap at Dry Martini Barcelona, one of the city's most iconic cocktail bars with a legendary gin menu.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast or Forn de Sant Josep bakery nearby for Catalan pastries, pa amb tomàquet, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet spread or café lunch in Gràcia — try La Pepita for creative Catalan bocadillos and local wines
meals.dinner: Alkimia — Michelin-starred contemporary Catalan tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família private tour and Park Güell timed entry well in advance — both sell out quickly in August. August heat peaks in the afternoon; carry water and wear light clothing. Private car recommended between Sagrada Família and Park Güell for comfort.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour — a private guided morning walk through Barcelona's medieval heart. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city, the magnificent Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, the ancient Jewish Quarter (El Call), and hidden medieval courtyards. A private expert guide will reveal layers of history invisible to casual visitors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tapas and Wine Tour in El Born — transition seamlessly from the Gothic Quarter into the adjacent El Born neighborhood for a premium guided tapas crawl. Sample traditional Catalan pintxos, jamón ibérico, fresh seafood, and regional wines at curated stops including El Xampanyet and Bar del Pla. Explore the stunning Mercat de Santa Caterina and the El Born Cultural Centre.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop of El Nacional or the W Barcelona Sky Bar with views over the city and sea. Dinner at Cinc Sentits — another Michelin-starred gem offering a refined Catalan tasting menu with an exceptional natural wine list. After dinner, experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife with a VIP table booking at Pacha Barcelona or Opium on Passeig Marítim.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Cafè de l'Acadèmia near the Gothic Quarter — traditional Catalan breakfast with fresh juice
meals.lunch: Guided tapas and wine tour in El Born covers lunch — multiple tastings across 4–5 premium stops
meals.dinner: Cinc Sentits — Michelin-starred Catalan tasting menu; post-dinner VIP club entry included in nightlife package

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter morning tour — cobblestones are uneven. VIP nightclub table bookings for Pacha or Opium should be arranged 48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge. Clubs typically open at midnight and peak around 2–3 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Late, leisurely morning to recover from the previous night's festivities. Hotel spa session or rooftop pool relaxation. Optional: private architecture-focused walking tour of Eixample's Modernista buildings including Casa Lleó Morera, Palau del Baró de Quadras, and the lesser-known gems along Carrer d'Enric Granados — a pedestrianized boulevard perfect for a slow architectural stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private interior visit to Casa Milà (La Pedrera) — Gaudí's extraordinary apartment building. Book a premium after-hours or exclusive guided access experience to explore the undulating rooftop terrace with its iconic warrior chimneys, the Espai Gaudí exhibition, and a restored period apartment. This is one of Barcelona's most architecturally significant interiors.
day_by_day.evening: Nightclub Experience on Passeig Marítim — Barcelona's legendary beachfront club strip. Begin with sunset cocktails at a beach chiringuito, followed by dinner at Bestial (beneath the W Hotel, overlooking the beach). Then proceed to an iconic club such as Shôko or Catwalk for a full VIP nightlife experience with bottle service and premium table placement.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast — full à la carte service, fresh-squeezed juices, artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — premium tapas institution beloved by locals and visitors alike; try the montaditos and fresh seafood
meals.dinner: Bestial Restaurant at Passeig Marítim — Mediterranean cuisine with beachfront terrace dining before the club experience

day_by_day.notes: La Pedrera premium access or after-hours 'La Pedrera by Night' event should be booked in advance — it includes live music on the rooftop and is a truly magical experience in summer. Dress code for clubs is smart-casual to elegant; avoid sportswear. Hotel concierge can arrange VIP entry and bottle service packages.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — private rooftop breakfast at the hotel or a slow café morning at Federal Café in Sant Antoni. Optional last architectural discovery: visit the Palau de la Música Catalana (a UNESCO World Heritage Modernista concert hall by Lluís Domènech i Montaner) for a guided interior tour — a stunning counterpoint to Gaudí's work and often overlooked by visitors.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisurely farewell afternoon in Eixample — last-minute premium shopping along Passeig de Gràcia (Loewe, Massimo Dutti, local design boutiques). Visit the Fundació Antoni Tàpies for world-class contemporary Catalan art in a beautiful Modernista building. Enjoy a final glass of cava at a terrace café before departure preparations.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at ABaC Restaurant & Hotel (3 Michelin stars, Tibidabo area — 15 min by private car) — Chef Jordi Cruz's flagship restaurant is among Spain's finest, offering an extraordinary avant-garde tasting menu. A truly memorable final dinner. Private chauffeur transfer back to hotel and then to airport if departing late, or overnight rest before next-day departure.

meals.breakfast: Rooftop hotel breakfast or Federal Café — specialty coffee, avocado toast, Catalan cheeses
meals.lunch: Bodega Sepúlveda in Eixample — traditional Catalan wine bar with outstanding charcuterie and local cheeses; perfect relaxed farewell lunch
meals.dinner: ABaC Restaurant — 3 Michelin stars, avant-garde tasting menu with premium wine pairing; reserve months in advance

day_by_day.notes: ABaC is the crown jewel of Barcelona fine dining — reservations are extremely competitive and should be made as early as possible. Confirm departure logistics with hotel concierge. Consider purchasing a bottle of local Penedès cava or Priorat wine as a souvenir from a specialist wine shop on Carrer de Consell de Cent.
